children: rose 0.14% premarket after Needham reiterated a Buy rating and $750 price target, following its examination of the fixed automatic license plate reader market. Privacy scrutiny of ALPR systems has weighed on the sector, and contract cancellations at Flock Safety have surged this year after public opposition to data sharing and governance policies. Axon shares fell 8.52% Tuesday and are down more than 14% over the past week.

Flock holds 82% of the US fixed ALPR market with 112,000 cameras in the field as of this week. Needham expects that market to dry up through 2026 and likely 2027, until vendors and law enforcement can convince citizens their governance strategies protect individual rights. Its research found only a handful of customers switching to Axon cameras, with the more common outcome being cameras shut off entirely.

Needham doesn't view ALPR as central to Axon's 2026 guidance or its 2028 financial targets, calling the fixed opportunity a modest input to its three-year model. Axon reported second quarter revenue of $904 million, up 35%, and raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 32% to 34%. Needham expects Axon to gain share against Flock in real-time crime center software and drones, citing brand reputation and a broader ecosystem.

title: Needham Backs Axon After a 14% Week on ALPR Fears
